🚀 Learning Focus

Recognise food spoilage, investigate food preservation methods and their role in food supply, and manage biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste responsibly for a sustainable life.

💡

Big Idea (Understanding)

🍞 8.1 Food Spoilage

Recognising spoiled food helps us make safe food choices in our daily lives. Changes in colour and texture, unpleasant smell, mould and slimy surfaces can be signs of spoilage caused by microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi.

Real-life situation: Check food carefully before eating and tell an adult if it smells unusual, changes appearance or shows mould. Never taste food to test whether it has spoiled.

🥫 8.2 Food Preservation

Food preservation helps keep food safe, reduces food waste and ensures a continuous food supply. Methods control factors that affect microorganism growth, such as temperature, water availability, air and acidity.

Real-life situation: Drying, salting, pickling, freezing or boiling can be used to preserve suitable foods. Some foods can be preserved using a combination of methods, such as salting and drying fish.

♻️ 9.1 Waste Material

The way we manage waste in our daily lives affects the environment and contributes to a sustainable future. Biodegradable waste can be decomposed by microorganisms; non-biodegradable waste does not decompose easily.

Real-life situation: Separate waste, reuse and recycle suitable materials, compost food scraps and dry leaves, and dispose of hazardous waste properly.

🛡️ Safety first: Do not taste food used in spoilage observations. Do not handle mouldy food directly; ask a teacher or adult to prepare sealed samples. Use knives, hot water and preservation equipment only with adult supervision. Wash hands after activities.
